title: Midsummer and a letter home
goal: Celebrate your first Swedish Midsummer, then write about it: a friendly email, a polite complaint — and a look back at everything Svenska 102 has given you.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Midsommarafton vid Siljan
dialogs.intro: Midsummer Eve. Dian, Oskar and Jonas have come with Elin to her parents' summer cabin by Lake Siljan in Dalarna, the heartland of Swedish Midsummer. Anna and Lars meet them on the porch.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Välkomna, och glad midsommar! Har ni hittat hit utan problem?
lines.id: Welcome, and happy Midsummer! Did you find your way here all right?
lines.literal: welcome(pl), and glad midsummer! have you(pl) found to-here without problem?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Ja, tack. Vi tog tåget till Leksand och sedan bussen. Vilken utsikt över sjön!
lines.id: Yes, thanks. We took the train to Leksand and then the bus. What a view of the lake!
lines.literal: yes, thanks. we took train-the to Leksand and then bus-the. what view over lake-the!

lines.speaker: Lars:
lines.text: Siljan är som vackrast i juni. Nu ska vi klä midsommarstången innan grannarna kommer.
lines.id: Siljan is at its most beautiful in June. Now we're going to dress the maypole before the neighbors come.
lines.literal: Siljan is as most-beautiful in June. now shall we dress midsummer-pole-the before neighbors-the come.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Hur gör man? Jag har bara sett det på bilder.
lines.id: How do you do it? I've only seen it in pictures.
lines.literal: how do one? I have only seen it on pictures.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Den kläs med björklöv och blommor, och sedan reses den på ängen klockan tre.
lines.id: It's covered with birch leaves and flowers, and then it's raised in the meadow at three.
lines.literal: it is-dressed with birch-leaves and flowers, and then is-raised it on meadow-the clock three.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Och sedan dansar alla Små grodorna runt den. Du ska få se!
lines.id: And then everyone dances "The Little Frogs" around it. You'll see!
lines.literal: and then dance all Small frogs-the around it. you shall get see!

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Man hoppar som en groda. Det är ju helt galet, om man tänker efter.
lines.id: You hop like a frog. It's completely crazy, if you think about it.
lines.literal: one hops like a frog. it is as-you-know completely crazy, if one thinks after.

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Galet men roligt. Och efter dansen blir det sill, färskpotatis och jordgubbar.
lines.id: Crazy but fun. And after the dance there's herring, new potatoes and strawberries.
lines.literal: crazy but fun. and after dance-the becomes it herring, fresh-potato and strawberries.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Om mina vänner i Indonesien såg mig nu, skulle de inte tro sina ögon!
lines.id: If my friends in Indonesia could see me now, they wouldn't believe their eyes!
lines.literal: if my friends in Indonesia saw me now, would they not believe their eyes!

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Du ska väl skicka en bild till din mamma?
lines.id: You'll send a picture to your mom, won't you?
lines.literal: you shall surely send a picture to your mom?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Ja, och jag har lovat att skriva ett långt mejl till henne ikväll.
lines.id: Yes, and I've promised to write her a long email tonight.
lines.literal: yes, and I have promised to write a long email to her tonight.

lines.speaker: Lars:
lines.text: Och i natt ska du plocka sju sorters blommor och lägga dem under kudden.
lines.id: And tonight you're to pick seven kinds of flowers and put them under your pillow.
lines.literal: and in night shall you pick seven kinds' flowers and lay them under pillow-the.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Då drömmer du om personen du ska gifta dig med. Det säger traditionen i alla fall.
lines.id: Then you'll dream about the person you're going to marry. That's what tradition says, anyway.
lines.literal: then dream you about person-the you shall marry yourself with. it says tradition-the in all cases.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Men man får inte säga ett enda ord när man plockar dem!
lines.id: But you're not allowed to say a single word while you pick them!
lines.literal: but one may not say a single word when one picks them!

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Det klarar jag nog inte. Jag pratar ju hela tiden — och på svenska nu, dessutom!
lines.id: I probably can't manage that. I talk all the time — and in Swedish now, too!
lines.literal: that manage I probably not. I talk as-you-know whole time-the — and on Swedish now, besides!

notes: **Glad midsommar!** — the greeting of the day, like *God jul* at Christmas. *Midsommarafton* (Midsummer Eve) always falls on a **Friday** between June 19 and 25, and it's the real celebration; Saturday, *midsommardagen*, is mostly for recovering. **glahd MID-som-mahr**.

**Har ni hittat hit?** — Unit 17 at work: *hit* (to here) because finding your way is movement. Anna would say *Bor ni **här**?* for location. And *ni* (you, plural) gets the plural *Välkomn**a***: one guest is *Välkommen*, several are *Välkomna*.

**Som vackrast** — "at its most beautiful". *Som* + superlative is a fixed frame for "at its best": *som bäst*, *som varmast*, *som vackrast*. *Siljan är som vackrast i juni* = June is when Siljan looks its best.

**Den kläs… och sedan reses den** — two s-passives from Unit 5, the way you'd hear them in instructions: *kläs* (is dressed) from *klä*, *reses* (is raised) from *resa*. Careful: *resa* means "to raise" here, not "to travel". The same verb, two meanings — context decides.

**Om mina vänner såg mig nu, skulle de…** — the hypothetical from Unit 14: *om* + past tense, then *skulle* + base form. English does the same: "If my friends **saw** me now, they **would**…". And **sina ögon** — *sina* because the eyes belong to the subject, *de*.

**Personen du ska gifta dig med** — *som* has been dropped (Unit 13: *som* can go when it's the object), and *gifta sig med* (to marry) is the reflexive from Unit 7. One small sentence, two units of review. **I alla fall** means "anyway, at least": **i AHL-lah fahl**.

grammars.title: Writing messages: openings and closings
body: Swedish written communication is famously informal. *Hej* works almost everywhere — to a friend, a teacher, even a company or a government agency. What changes with the register is mainly the closing.
after: The old-style openings *Bästa Lena* or *Kära Lena* (Dear Lena) still exist, but they sound either very formal or very affectionate. For most emails, *Hej Lena!* is exactly right.
Useful middle phrases: *Hoppas att allt är bra med dig* (I hope all is well), *Tack för senast!* (Thanks for last time!), *Tack på förhand* (Thanks in advance), *Hör av dig!* (Get in touch!).

grammars.title: A polite complaint in four steps
body: A Swedish complaint is short, factual and calm. Swedes rarely raise their voices in writing; the politer you are, the more seriously you're taken.

head: Step
What you do
Phrases
rows: Jag **skulle vilja** ha ersättning / få pengarna tillbaka.

after: *Skulle vilja* (would like) is the polite form of *vill* from Unit 14. *Jag vill ha pengarna tillbaka* is clear but blunt; *Jag skulle vilja få pengarna tillbaka* is the same demand in a suit and tie.

blocks.text: A friendly email: Dian writes to her teacher

blocks.title: Ämne: Midsommar i Dalarna
items: Hej Lena!
Hoppas att du har haft en skön midsommar. Jag firade min första midsommar hos Elins föräldrar i Dalarna, och det var fantastiskt.
Vi klädde stången, dansade Små grodorna och åt sill och jordgubbar. Det regnade faktiskt inte en enda gång!
Tack vare din kurs i våras förstod jag nästan alla sångerna. Tack för en jättebra termin!
Vi ses i augusti när höstterminen börjar.
Varma hälsningar,
Dian

blocks.text: Notice the shape: greeting, a friendly wish (*Hoppas att…*), what happened (past tense), a thank-you, a look ahead, closing. *Tack vare* means "thanks to" and is followed by a noun: *tack vare din kurs*, *tack vare vädret*.
A polite complaint: the late train

blocks.title: Ämne: Försenat tåg den 19 juni
items: Hej,
Jag skriver angående mitt tåg från Stockholm till Leksand den 19 juni, med avgång klockan 10.12. Tåget blev tre timmar försenat, och vi fick ingen information under resan.
Enligt era villkor har resenärer rätt till ersättning när ett tåg är mer än en timme försenat. Jag skulle därför vilja ha ersättning för förseningen. Mitt bokningsnummer är K7X4M2.
Tack på förhand.
Med vänliga hälsningar
Dian

blocks.text: All four steps are there: what it's about (*angående*), the facts (*den 19 juni*, *tre timmar försenat*), what she wants (*skulle vilja ha ersättning*), a polite close. Two new useful words: **enligt** (according to) and **rätt till** (the right to, entitled to): *Du har rätt till ersättning*.

Midsummer is, for many Swedes, the most important holiday of the year — more than Christmas for some. People leave the cities for the countryside, wear flower crowns, dance around the maypole, eat herring and the first strawberries of the summer, and sing before every shot of schnapps. Dalarna, around Lake Siljan, is where the celebrations are most traditional.

blocks.title: Svenska 102: can you do this now?
items: Tell a story in the past with time clauses (*när*, *innan*, *efter att*) and time expressions (*i fredags*, *för två år sedan*).
Use particle verbs, *-s* verbs, reflexive verbs and the s-passive without stopping to think.
Explain why (*eftersom*, *därför*), compare (*lika … som*, *mer … än*), imagine (*om jag vann skulle jag…*) and report (*hon sa att…*).
Get the small words right: *i/på/om* with time, *hem/hemma*, *ju/väl/nog*.
Handle real life: a café shift, a doctor's visit, an email and a complaint.
If most of this feels comfortable, you're ready for Svenska 103 — and for Dian's next adventure in Göteborg.
